items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I was able to get in touch with 'Casspoil'. He was actually an amateur drummer, but he studied the drums and could play very well. As luck would have it, he was free to join and arrived in Bern that afternoon in time for the job that night.

ctx.x: Later, I read an interview that Zutty gave to a jazz magazine that he had been working with me in Europe for peanuts which was to say that I paid him a small salary. He had 250 dollars a week with me which was a good salary anywhere in 1952 and there are musicians in the U.S.A. today that don't make a salary like that for a week's work. And he didn't mention that on the tour he did in Europe with Mezz Mezrow, he only had 200 dollars a week. And that's a fact that I know is true.

When I was in Geneva with Jack Dieval, I had met a young Swiss drummer called Caspoil whose real name was Pascal Jeanmairet. He had left me use his bicycle during my stay of one month, and I rode it around town most every day. So when I found out that Zutty had left, with the help of my friend Felix Debrit, I was able to get in touch with "Casspoil". He was actually an amateur drummer, but he studied the drums and could play very well. As luck would have it, he was free to join and arrived in Bern that afternoon…

I had signed a contract with Miriam Burton only for the tour because I knew that she was not the kind of singer for a night-club. Miriam knew another American Negro girl that was in Paris with her sister. Miriam knew that she could not be hired for the Chikito, so she sent this girl to see me. Her name was Suzette Aimes. Suzette had a very nice low voice and her approach to singing jazz was quite new and could be compared with the way some of the girls are singing today such as Aretha Franklin, etc. But she was…
